content: The specific dosing recommendations for Airelle, Black Whortles, Burren Myrtle, and Bilberry in combination are as follows: oral administration of 20-60 grams per day or 160 mg taken orally twice daily. These preparations typically contain 25% anthocyanosides. Alternatively, one cup of the preparation can be taken orally, or 1 gram of dried leaf can be steeped in 150 ml of water for consumption. For topical applications, a 10% decoction can be applied as needed. Dried berries can also be boiled in water to prepare a decoction. These substances are indicated for the management of angina, atherosclerosis, circulatory problems, degenerative retinal conditions, diarrhea, mouth and throat inflammation (when used topically), retinopathy, and varicose veins. Clinical studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of bilberry in treating diarrhea and retinopathy. Potential adverse effects include cachexia, anemia, and icterus. High doses have been associated with excitation in animal studies. No significant interactions or contraindications have been reported. Regarding pregnancy and lactation, there is no specific categorization available (Pregnancy Category: N/A; Lactation: N/A). However, these substances are generally considered acceptable for use. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
